In what case is this said? With soft items such as sheets and garments; but pillows and cushions that are hard, and there is no concern lest a thread wrap upon him—it is permitted to sleep on them, provided his flesh does not touch them. In what case is this said? When they are empty and placed on a wooden or stone bench; but if they are full, or even if empty when they are placed on a bed or on straw—it is forbidden, because it bends beneath him and wraps upon his flesh. {Rama: And some say all this applies to kilayim d'oraisa; but with kilayim d'rabbanan that are hard, it is permitted to sit on them in every case, since when they are hard it is only d'rabbanan—they did not decree on hard items (Rashba siman 962). Nevertheless, l'chatchila one should not make items of kilayim (Kol Bo).}
